title: Explore Bhutan with FREE Taktsang Monastery Tour
highlights: Explore Bhutan's rich traditions with visits to ancient dzongs, vibrant markets, and sacred monasteries, capped with breathtaking treks through lush valleys.
Step into Bhutan’s second-oldest fortress-monastery, Punakha Dzong famed for its grand halls, intricate woodwork, and iconic location between two rivers.
Head to the 17th-century Drukgyel Dzong, a fortress that commemorates Bhutan’s victory over Tibet, with vistas of Mount Jomolhari in the background.
Ascend through lush pine forests to reach Tiger's Nest Monastery, where tales of Guru Rinpoche's flight on a tigress come alive.
overview:
About the tour:
Embark on an unforgettable Bhutan tour weaving through the vibrant streets of Thimphu, the tranquil landscapes of Punakha and Gangtey, and culminating in the awe-inspiring hike to Paro Taktsang. This journey seamlessly blends tradition with modernity, offering a rich cultural experience against the backdrop of Bhutan's stunning natural beauty. This tour promises a tapestry of memories, connecting you deeply with the heart and soul of Bhutan.

know_before_you_go: Cancellation After Rescheduling: Clients who reschedule their tours or treks but later decide to cancel will be subject to our standard cancellation policy. Any rescheduling fees paid will be non-refundable.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

In cases of force majeure events (e.g., natural disasters, political unrest, or other unforeseeable circumstances), [Thrillophilia] reserves the right to reschedule tours & treks or offer alternative itineraries to ensure the safety and well-being of clients and staff.
Please note that prices are dynamic and may change in the peak season and on blackout dates.
Any breakage or damage of any items in the stay property will be charged at actuals.
Please note that the timings and duration of pick-up and drop-off transfers may vary based on certain factors like traffic, weather conditions, natural calamities, etc.
Prices may fluctuate with any change in services/hotels. The difference in the cost shall be borne by the client in case of any amendment in the package due to an increase in the number of guests.

If in case any traveller wants to or decides to leave the trip in the middle, all the expenses from the point onwards will be borne by the traveller. Neither the operator nor Thrillophilia will be held responsible for such decisions or for any refund.
It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.

Rescheduling Policy for Private (Standard & Deluxe Package) & Group Bookings: 1) If rescheduling is made 7 days after the booking date till 15 days prior to the date of travel then 30.0% of the total tour cost will be charged as rescheduling fees. | 2) If rescheduling is made 0 days to 15 days before the date of travel then 100.0% of the total tour cost will be charged as cancellation fees. | 3) If bookings are made 15 days before the date of travel no rescheduling & modifications will be made.
Rescheduling Policy for Private (Super Deluxe) & Hotel Specific Bookings: No modification or rescheduling will be catered. A standard cancellation policy will be applicable for such cases.
Please note that nn Saturdays and Sundays, the Phuentsholing Bhutan permit office remains closed.
Please note, the provided vehicle is for point-to-point services only. Any extra usage beyond the itinerary will incur additional charges, payable in cash on the spot.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.desc: Arrive at the New Jalpaiguri Railway Station/Bagdogra International Airport and board your transfer to Phuntsholing, passing through quaint villages and tea estates. Upon arrival in Bhutan, check in at your hotel and relax. Later, explore iconic attractions like the Karbandi Monastery or the local markets on your own before heading back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get driven to Thimphu after completing your immigration process in order to obtain a travel permit. Upon arrival, check in and relax before exploring the locality on your own. Witness the Buddha Dordenma statue, standing at an impressive 177 feet. Take a stroll through the beautiful Royal Botanical Garden. Also, visit the bustling Handicrafts Market to shop for souvenirs before returning to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Start your day with a transfer for a Thimphu sightseeing tour. Visit the Folk Heritage Museum, where you can explore a traditional Bhutanese farmhouse and gain insights into rural life. Next, head to the Jungshi Handmade Paper Factory to witness the traditional art of paper-making and observe artisans crafting paper using ancient techniques. Explore a few more places before getting transferred to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass | Punakha Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Once you’ve checked out, board your transfer to Punakha, passing through Dochula Pass, where the beautiful mountain scenery and fluttering prayer flags create a tranquil setting. Once you reach Punakha, visit Chimi Lhakhang, a temple famous for its fertility rituals, followed by Punakha Dzong, which once served as Bhutan’s administrative centre and fortress. Upon arrival in Punakha, check in at the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: On this day, check out of the hotel and get transferred to Paro, passing through various Bhutanese villages. Stop at Simtokha Dzong to admire its ancient Buddha statues and exquisite paintings that depict tales from Buddhist mythology. Continue your journey to Paro and, once you arrive, explore Drukgyel Dzong, a historic fortress celebrated for its role in Bhutan's victory over Tibetan invaders. After your sightseeing, get driven to check in at the hotel for a relaxing overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: As a new day welcomes you, get driven to Ta Dzong, which houses an amazing collection of Bhutanese artefacts and offers scenic views of the Paro Valley. Next, explore Paro Rinpung Dzong, a stunning fortress known for its rich history and architecture. From there, transfer to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang (starting point) for a hike to the Taktsang Monastery on a cliffside, a renowned sacred site perched high on a cliff. After your trek, get driven to the hotel to relax overnight.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and board your pre-booked transfer to Phuntsholing. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and spend the remaining day at leisure by exploring Phuntsholing’s highlights on your own. Visit the Bhutan Gate for a glimpse of Bhutan's unique architecture, stroll along the Torsa River to enjoy the scenic riverbank views, and head to Zangto Pelri Lhakhang, a temple dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. After your exploration, return to the hotel on your own for a night stay.
